question: The nature of the bond formed in aliphatic carbon compounds is:
solution: The correct answer is __**covalent**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **nature of the bond** in aliphatic carbon compounds is primarily **covalent**. Covalent bonds are formed due to the sharing of electron pairs between atoms. • In aliphatic compounds, carbon atoms form bonds with hydrogen or other carbon atoms through **single (sigma), double (pi), or triple bonds**, which are all covalent in nature. • Covalent bonding allows carbon to achieve a stable electron configuration by completing its **octet** (8 electrons in the outer shell). • Aliphatic compounds include structures like alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes, all of which are based on covalent bonding within their molecular framework. • This type of bonding is responsible for the stability, reactivity, and various physical and chemical properties of aliphatic carbon compounds.
